title: Finite-type relative ampleness has a common very ample power
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $X$ quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Here $\mathcal M$ is $f$-ample when $f$ is quasi-compact and, for every affine open $V\subset X$, the restriction to $f^{-1}(V)$ is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Say that $\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$ is relatively very ample over $X$ if there are a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ and an immersion $i:Y\to\mathbf P_X(\mathcal E)$ over $X$ such that $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$, with the projective bundle as in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Then $\mathcal M$ is $f$-ample if and only if $\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$ is relatively very ample for some $n\ge1$, equivalently for every sufficiently large $n$. Moreover, whenever $\mathcal N$ is relatively very ample for a quasi-compact morphism $g:Z\to X$, the morphism $g$ is quasi-separated, the evaluation map $g^*g_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal N$ is surjective, and the associated map $Z\to\mathbf P_X(g_*\mathcal N)$ is an immersion.

source.place: Tag 01VU, lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample, using Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample (especially clause (4) evaluation surjection and immersion), together with Definition 01VM.

proof.text: First prove the local-to-global construction needed below. Let $g:Z\to X$ be quasi-compact, let $N$ be invertible, and suppose an open cover $(V_j)$ of $X$ has witnesses $i_j:Z_j=g^{-1}(V_j)\to\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)$ with $i_j$ an immersion and $i_j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N|_{Z_j}$. No finite-type hypothesis on $E_j$ is used. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], the projective-bundle projections are separated. Every immersion is separated: factor it as a closed immersion and an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the former is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], and the latter is a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], so its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion. Composition preserves separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Consequently each $g_j:Z_j\to V_j$ is separated. The opens $Z_j\times_{V_j}Z_j$ cover $Z\times_XZ$ and restrict $\Delta_g$ to $\Delta_{g_j}$. Closed-immersion locality [lem-weil-pbc-closed-finite-etale-zariski-local](1) therefore makes $g$ separated; [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), separatedness paragraph; Tag 01VQ (lemma-relatively-very-ample-separated).

proof.text: Put $F=g_*N$. Invertibility makes $N$ quasi-coherent [def-sc-invertible-module], so the quasi-compactness of $g$ and quasi-separatedness from Step 1 give quasi-coherence of $F$ by [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh]. The quotient interpretation [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] associates to $i_j$ a surjection $q_j:g_j^*E_j\to N|_{Z_j}$. Adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $\alpha_j:E_j\to(g_j)_*(N|_{Z_j})=F|_{V_j}$, the equality holding sectionwise. The adjunction identity says $q_j=\varepsilon|_{Z_j}\circ g_j^*\alpha_j$, where $\varepsilon:g^*F\to N$ is evaluation. Since this composite is surjective, $\varepsilon$ is surjective over every $Z_j$, hence everywhere. The same quotient interpretation now constructs $r:Z\to\mathbf P_X(F)$, with $r^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N$, from precisely this evaluation quotient.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), evaluation factorization display.

proof.text: Here is the immersion check, including the comparison omitted in 01VR. On $P_j=\mathbf P_X(F)|_{V_j}=\mathbf P_{V_j}(F|_{V_j})$, compose the pullback of $\alpha_j$ with the tautological quotient to obtain $p_j^*E_j\to\mathcal O_{P_j}(1)$. Its surjectivity locus $U_j$ is open: locally trivialize the target line, and take the union of the nonvanishing loci of the images of local sections of $E_j$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. On $U_j$ the quotient property [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] gives $h_j:U_j\to\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)$. Step 2's equation $q_j=\varepsilon g_j^*\alpha_j$ implies that $r|_{Z_j}$ factors through $U_j$: the pulled-back composite quotient is surjective at every point. Naturality of the quotient bijection then gives $h_j\circ(r|_{Z_j})=i_j$, since both morphisms correspond to the identical quotient $q_j$, not merely to the same line bundle. By [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation], $Z_j\to U_j$ is an immersion, and its composite into $P_j$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). The $P_j$ cover $\mathbf P_X(F)$; [lem-zl-immersion-near-image-locality] proves that $r$ is an immersion. Thus Steps 1--3 prove global very ampleness from local witnesses. Taking the cover with its single member $X$ also proves the asserted evaluation clause, including quasi-coherence of $g_*N$, without any finite-type assumption on $g$.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open U_j and the omitted factorization verification.

proof.text: Assume now that $M$ is $f$-ample. Choose a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_{a=1}^mV_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Set $Y_a=f^{-1}(V_a)$, $L_a=M|_{Y_a}$. Each $L_a$ is ample by the hypothesis. The finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] supplies local finite type of $Y_a\to V_a$ and quasi-compactness of $Y_a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] to obtain an integer $b_a\ge1$ and an immersion $j_a:Y_a\to\mathbf P^{r_a}_{V_a}$ with $j_a^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_a^{\otimes b_a}$. The Proj presentation in that node agrees with this projective space and its twist by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. If $Y_a$ is empty one may simply take $b_a=1$, $r_a=0$ and the empty immersion.

source.place: Tag 01VU (lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample), finite affine covering; Tag 01VS (lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S), first paragraph, one-power construction.

proof.text: For each $a$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] applied to $L_a$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_{Y_a}$ gives $c_a\ge0$ such that $L_a^{\otimes e}$ is generated by finitely many global sections whenever $e\ge c_a$. The structure module is quasi-coherent and of finite type because locally it is free of rank one. Increase $c_a$ to at least $1$. For $d\ge b_a+c_a$, choose generators of $L_a^{\otimes(d-b_a)}$; their surjective quotient of a finite free sheaf defines $j'_a:Y_a\to\mathbf P^{t_a-1}_{V_a}$ with $(j'_a)^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_a^{\otimes(d-b_a)}$ by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. When $Y_a$ is nonempty its generating family is nonempty; for the empty scheme choose one zero section. The pair $(j_a,j'_a)$ is an immersion because its composite with the first projection is $j_a$, by [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation]. Compose it with the Segre closed immersion [lem-chow-segre]; the result is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). By [def-chow-segre], Segre coordinates are the products of the two sets of coordinates, so its pulled-back $\mathcal O(1)$ is $j_a^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes(j'_a)^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_a^{\otimes d}$, using the tensor/pullback identifications [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. This proves relative very ampleness of every $L_a^{\otimes d}$ for $d\ge b_a+c_a$.

source.place: Tag 01VS (lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S), second paragraph; Properties Tag 01Q3 (proposition-characterize-ample), global-generation clause; Constructions Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding).

proof.text: Take $d_0=\max(\{1\}\cup\{b_a+c_a:1\le a\le m\})$. For every $d\ge d_0$, Step 5 supplies local projective-space witnesses for $M^{\otimes d}$ over all $V_a$; projective spaces are projective bundles by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Since $f$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], apply the construction of Steps 1--3 with $g=f$ and $N=M^{\otimes d}$. It gives an immersion $Y\to\mathbf P_X(f_*M^{\otimes d})$ pulling back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $M^{\otimes d}$. Thus every $d\ge d_0$ is relatively very ample. The maximum includes $1$ so the same argument covers an empty base and an empty covering; then $Y$ is empty as well.

source.place: Tag 01VU (lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample), common bound and application of 01VR.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $N=M^{\otimes n}$, $n\ge1$, is relatively very ample, witnessed by $i:Y\to\mathbf P_X(E)$ and $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N$. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], $i$ corresponds to a surjection $q:f^*E\to N$. Set $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}(E)$, with its quasi-coherent graded construction [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] extends the adjoint of $q$ to a graded map $\mathcal A\to f_*(\bigoplus_{k\ge0}N^{\otimes k})$; its degree-$k$ formula sends a product $e_1\cdots e_k$ to $q(e_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes q(e_k)$. Adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{k\ge0}N^{\otimes k}$. The degree-one surjection makes $U(\psi)=Y$, and the quotient geometry identifies $r_{N,\psi}$ with the original immersion $i$. As $f$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [lem-trf-graded-immersion-ample-criterion] implies that $N$ is ample over every affine open of $X$.

source.place: Tag 01VN (lemma-ample-very-ample), proof via Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), (6) implies (1); Tag 01VU, reverse implication.

proof.text: For every affine open $V\subseteq X$, put $T=f^{-1}(V)$ and $L=M|_T$. Step 7 makes $L^{\otimes n}$ ample, so $T$ is quasi-compact. Given $y\in T$, choose $k\ge1$ and $s\in\Gamma(T,(L^{\otimes n})^{\otimes k})$ with $y\in T_s$ and $T_s$ affine, by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Tensor reassociation views this very same section as a section of $L^{\otimes nk}$, with the same germs and hence the same nonvanishing locus; $nk\ge1$. The definition therefore says $L$ is ample. As $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], this is $f$-ampleness of $M$. Finally, all sufficiently large positive powers being very ample implies that one positive power is very ample by choosing $d\ge\max(1,d_0)$, while the forward implication is Step 6. This completes both equivalences and the evaluation assertion proved in Steps 1--3.

split_report.summary: Preserved the complete statement and proved it in eight steps following 01VU/01VR. Reused the existing affine-base one-power immersion, eventual finite global generation, Segre, immersion cancellation/locality and quasi-coherent pushforward nodes. Expanded the 01VR rational-map comparison and used a finite affine maximum for the uniform bound. Added only two general statement-only prerequisites: projective-bundle quotient geometry for arbitrary quasi-coherent modules and the arbitrary graded-algebra Proj-immersion ampleness criterion. Proved positive-power reflection directly from the definition.
